item.title: Canadian pump prices creep higher as Mideast fighting escalates
item.description: Fuel prices tend to ease off around this time of year, but one industry expert says drivers should expect no such relief this time.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: CALGARY — Fuel prices tend to ease off around this time of year, but one industry expert says drivers should expect no such relief this time. The high-demand summer driving season winds down after Labour Day and refineries will soon switch to producing cheaper winter fuels. But international crude oil prices have surged above US$100 a barrel as fighting once again escalates in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route out of the Persian Gulf. Price-tracking website Gasbuddy.com says the national average for a litre of regular unleaded gasoline in Canada is almost $1.80, a more than three-cent jump from a day earlier. Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at Gasbuddy, says pump prices could further creep up as high as $1.85 a litre in the next week or two. He says diesel prices are also seeing a surge at a particularly bad time for farmers who are in the middle of their fall harvest. --- Lauren Krugel, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 9, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Gordon Reid, President & CEO, Goodreid Investment Counsel Focus: U.S. Equities

Top Picks: Dycom , Verizon , WESCO International MARKET OUTLOOK: The market is quietly rotating, away from the drivers of the last couple of years, namely communication service and technology stocks to more defensive issues that have been under owned, particularly healthcare. The result is serious stock action under the surface but on the face of things, large capitalization indexes are steady. The rotation appears to us to be in the latter stages, based on technical indicators and valuation but, as we have witnessed over the past year, the macro landscape is changing. A year ago, it was almost universally accepted that the next move in central bank interest rates would be in a downward direction. Now the opposite is true. Adding to the intrigue are the upcoming mid-term elections in the United States, which potentially could neuter the current U.S. administration. For now, we are preaching and practising balance in our portfolios. Goodreid’s U.S. large cap portfolio is benefitting from an under weighted position in mega cap tech in favour of a more defensive posture, while the U.S. small cap portfolio, a big beneficiary over the past couple of years of outstanding results within artificial intelligence (AI) related industrial names, is taking a breather. Market-moving news, fast:  Get the BNN Bloomberg App now Sign up for the Market Call Top Picks newsletter at  bnnbloomberg.ca/newsletters TOP PICKS: Gordon Reid's Top Picks: Dycom, Verizon & WESCO International Gordon Reid, President & CEO of Goodreid Investment Counsel, shares his top stock picks to watch in the market.

Dycom (DY NYSE) Dycom is recognized as a second derivative AI stock, as it supports hyper-scalers in providing the latest connectivity across North America. This issue has suffered recently along with the entire space, but we note that earnings are accelerating, and revisions are positive while valuations become increasingly more attractive. Although financial progress tends to be lumpy because of weather disruptions and uneven capital allocations from the large telecom companies, we believe this issue will again be priced with a premium valuation. Verizon (VZ NYSE) Verizon has performed well under the more entrepreneurial direction of Dan Schulman, former CEO at PayPal. Mobility and broadband divisions are growing well and under the new model cashflow is expanding because of a volume-based versus a subsidy-based approach. At less than 10 times forward earnings and paying a 5.6 per cent dividend yield this defensive gem is a stock for the times. WESCO International (WCC NYSE) Wesco is a distributor of electrical, industrial, and communication products. Once a staid industry, it is now a lynchpin in data center development, which account for about a quarter of its revenue. All in all, at just over 20 times earnings and mid-teens annual percentage growth of earnings ahead, we are excited.
